text: Diver Tops are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by various enemies, obtained as a quest reward after completing Save the Girl!, or be traded for with Elior. They are part of the Diver set along with the Diver Cap, Diver Gloves, Diver Bottoms and Diver Shoes.

Dolgan Outpost (Japanese: , Dorugan Kanshisai) is a landmark in . It is the second facility encountered in Sword Valley after Ged Fortress, and contains the control panel for the 4th Gate. It bears little resemblance to Ged Fortress beyond the same coloration. A defining feature of the outpost is the observatory on the second floor. A surprise and Timed Quest called Secure Dolgan Outpost is registered upon entering the area, requiring the party to defeat the Prudent Purson. There are two floors in the Dolgan Outpost; on the ground floor, there a few Mechon and the panel to unlocking the 4th Gate. On the upper floor are a few collectable items for the Sword Valley Collection and four Mechon,
Devil Cannons (Japanese: , Debirukyanon) are weapons in . They are ether rifles, and are usable by Sharla. They can be acquired as a quest reward.
The Dividing Line (Japanese: , Tekkai, Iron Slab) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a sword wielded by Dunban.
Disaster Cannons (Japanese: , Dezasutakyanon) are weapons in . They are rifles wielded by Sharla. They can be acquired by purchasing them at Colony 6 Shop 6 for 21,120 G.
The Digit 2 Plain (Japanese: , Hitosashi Gen'ya) is a landmark in . It is located on the lower level of Fallen Arm.

The Digit 5 Beach (Japanese: , Koyubi no Sunahama) is a location in . It is on the lower level of the Fallen Arm, south of Digit 5. The Ether Exhaust System can be accessed from the south-east of this beach. It is inhabited by Mechon and Krabbles.
Donnis (Japanese: , Dona) is a pureblooded High Entia in . He can be found in Alcamoth, next to the Ascension Hall transporter at night.
Destructive Bors (Japanese: , Shura no Bōrusu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 64 near the Telethia Bridge in Agniratha.

Devoted Arachnos (Japanese: , Shūshin no Supaido) are three quest exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Arachno family, and can be found at level 9 on the first floor of Vilia Lake in Tephra Cave. They only appear during the quest Clearing Obstructions, where two of them must be defeated.

Demon Web Fibres are rare materials in . They can be obtained from various high-level Arachno. They are also available for trade with Niranira and King Squeeze. According to their description, they are threads for weaving demon-wear, and are conscious and go for the tongue.

Dense Ansel Meat is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be dropped by Eryth Ansels in Eryth Sea or traded for in Alcamoth. According to their description, their mass increase tenfold in the mouth and it is considered best to take small bites. Three of them are required for Reversed Tastes.
Double Attack (Japanese: , Daburu Atakku) is a Gem in that grants a chance of attacking twice when auto-attacking. __TOC__
Divine Protect (Japanese: , Sokushi Teikō, Instant Death Resist) is a Gem in that grants a chance to resist Instant Death. __TOC__

Demon Slayer (Japanese: , Onizanba) is one of Dunban's physical arts in . It has a high base attack, and when it is used as a finishing blow, all active enemies within range are forcibly Toppled, regardless of whether they are suffering from Break, unless they are immune to Topple. This topple effect will only occur if the target enemy is killed by this art. A successful Demon Slayer will have a red gas resembling a face rise from the defeated enemy. Otherwise, it is only a red splash of gas.

Digit 1 (Japanese: , Kishin no Oyayubi) is a location in . It is the southernmost point on the Fallen Arm, south of the Giant Mechon Debris. It is the first finger of Mechonis' arm that was cut off in the battle against Bionis. Like the other Digits, it is curled up towards the sky. It is not directly next to the other digits, implying it is the thumb. A Heart-to-Heart - "Overcoming the Pain" - is located here.

Digit 2 (Japanese: , Kishin no Hitosashiyubi) is a location in . It is located on the Fallen Arm. It is the second finger of Mechonis' arm that was chopped off in the battle against Bionis. Like the other digits, it is curled up towards the sky. The second digit is curled more, as the tip is facing towards the hand's palm. This digit is the only one that can be climbed, allowing access to the Rotating Bulkhead and the Distant Fingertip. It is located west of Digit 2 Plain and Digit 1 Crevasse.

Digit 3 (Japanese: , Kishin no Nakayubi) is a location in . It is located on the Fallen Arm. It is the middle finger of the arm of Mechonis that was chopped off in its battle against Bionis. Like the other Digits, it is curled up towards the sky. This finger is pointed straighter than the others, as well as being longer than the others, as it should be to match a real hand. It is located west of the Connecting Bridge.

Digit 4 (Japanese: , Kishin no Kusuriyubi) is a location in . It is located on the Fallen Arm. It is the fourth finger of Mechonis' arm that was chopped off in the battle against Bionis. Like the other Digits, it is curled up towards the sky. It is located northwest of the Black Wreckage.

Digit 5 (Japanese: , Kishin no Koyubi) is a location in . It is the northernmost point on the lower level of the Fallen Arm, north of the Black Wreckage and north west of the Digit 5 Beach. Unlike the other fingers, it is almost completely submerged under water, and can only be reached by swimming round from the beach. There are no enemies here. It is the little finger of Mechonis' arm that was cut off in the battle against Bionis. Like the other Digits, it is curled up towards the sky. Since it is the little finger, it is much shorter than the other digits.

Distilling Active Ingredients (Japanese: , Yūkōseibun wo Chūshutsusuru) is a quest in . It can be received from Cherri at the Pollen Orb Storehouse in Frontier Village. It is only available if Cherri was chosen to be Dobadoba's apprentice during The Master's Successor (B route). This quest and Safer Energy are mutually exclusive. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.

The Divine Rock is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. The party is asked to retrieve it by Gorman, for For the Restoration. It is located at the very top of Spiral Valley on Bionis' Leg, behind the Immovable Gonzalez.

Dive Sobat (Japanese: , Daibu Sobatto, English dub: ) is one of Reyn's physical arts in . It may inflict Paralysis to the enemy. If used after Bone Upper, the enemy may be debuffed with Agility Down 25%. In , Nene has an identical version of this art called Chive Sobat.

Double Blade (Japanese: , Daburu Burēdo) is one of Fiora's arts in . This attack is very similar to Shulk's Back Slash and Riki's Sneaky attacks; it triples damage when attacking the enemy from behind.

Deluded Ignas (Japanese: , Mōshū no Igūna) are quest exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 24-25 above the Dark Swamp in Satorl Marsh. Five of them must be defeated for Kacha's quest The Giants' Key. After the five are defeated, the Giants' Key can be dug up on the plateau. They will drop the Igna Stone Pots needed for Nopon Determination.

Double Wind (Japanese: , Daburu Uindo) is one of Fiora's physical arts in . It strikes in a frontal arc against enemies in the attack area and increases Fiora's Tension. The affected enemies will also be knocked back by the attack.

Demonic Everflames are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only obtainable from two Dragons - the Demon King Dragonia and Avalanche Abaasy. According to their description, they are stones that emit a destructive heat that burns for all eternity. One is needed for Replica Monado 4.
Doom Hoxes are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Hox family, and can be found at level 24 near the Pod Depot in Colony 6.

Detox Brogs (Japanese: , Detokku Guroggu) are enemies in . They are members of the Brog family, and can be found from level 24-26 in Satorl Marsh near the Crown Tree. Defeating two of them is required to complete the Satorl Marsh's quest Monster Quest 1. They are the only enemy that drops White Brog Livers, which are needed for Cook-Off Counter Attack!.

The Dogmatic Gogol (Japanese: , Kairitsu no Gogōru) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It can be found at level 35 near the Place of Judgement in Satorl Marsh, only during the mutually-exclusive quests Talia's Research and Investigating Satorl. To complete either quest, the Dogmatic Gogol must be defeated. The Dogmatic Gogol is by far the weakest member of the Gogol family, with the next weakest members having levels in the seventies.

Diamond Brog Eyes are rare materials in . They can be dropped by Young Brogs in Tephra Cave, or traded for in Colony 9. According to their description, they are eyeballs that gleam like diamonds and it is possible to feel honored by the gaze from them. One is needed for the quest Replica Monado 5.

The Dios Pillar (Japanese: , Diosu no Hashira) is a location in . It is located on the first floor of Agniratha, south of the Helas Pillar. The Verification Device of the 3rd Control Platform at the top of the tower on 3F must be activated to complete Pillar Verification Devices and unlock the transporter to the Meyneth Shrine. The Wrathful Orobas can be found nearby.

Divisions are mechanics in . They are known as Unions (Japanese: , Yunion) in the Japanese version. There are eight different divisions within BLADE, each with their own objectives and support effects. Mission details can change based on Cross's choice of division, or the Division's membership of a party member. Cross was allowed to freely switch her/his affiliation, for a fee, while it was fixed for the other characters. This mechanic was discontinued with the shutdown of online services, alongside Division Support and Division Rewards. The choice of division affects the rate by which Division Points are earned, which in turn adds points to increasing BLADE Level. It was also possible to re

Doug Barrett (Japanese: , Dagu; English dub: ) is one of the eight main playable characters of . He is a Harrier and a member of the private military organization BLADE. He excels at all military skills, but is the most effective when it comes to piloting Skells. Doug is recruitable after Chapter 3. Prior to Earth's destruction he was part of the Coalition forces' Special Operations Heavy Armor Training Unit (commonly called the "Skelleton Crew") as Elma's subordinate. He has been Lao's comrade-in-arms since their days in the United States Army.

Director Arachnos (Japanese: , Direku Supaido) are two story exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Arachno family, and mostly command small groups of Arachnos. They are found in Tephra Cave, by a small unnamed pond between the Spring of Grief and Vilia Lake. After Shulk and Reyn find the traders' bodies, there is a story event battle in which they are attacked by two Director Arachnos and six Worker Arachnos. These story exclusive Director Arachnos are level 9 Kindred Enemies which drop no Treasure Chests, do not respawn, and detect by sight at a 120° angle, to a distance of 21 meters. There is a normal variant. These Director Arachno which appear in the same cavern after the event

Docile Ovis (Japanese: , Dōshiru Owisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Ovis family, and can be found at level 11-19 in Primordia, near FN Site 114 during the day. Defeating six of them is required during the Basic Mission Offing Ovis.

Disquiet (不安, Uneasiness) is an Event Track in Xenoblade Chronicles, composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 17 of disc 1 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is an ominous, unsettling theme that is heard in the following cutscenes: *Shulk's vision of Reyn being attacked by the Arachno Queen in Tephra Cave *The party discovers that Mechon are patrolling the Ether Mine *Alvis watches from a rock Lakeside in Makna Forest as Shulk and Reyn depart, shortly after helping Shulk defeat three Puera Telethia *Melia splits off from the party with her Imperial Guards after arriving at the Centre Gate to Alcamoth *Shulk's uneasy questions in Junks before the party leaves for th

Domestic Armored Suids (Japanese: , Teimu Āmā Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 5-9 at Seaswept Base in Primordia. They have been domesticated and armored by the Prone.

Desdemona, the Subterranean (Japanese: , Ankyo no Desudemona) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Scirpo and can be found at level 11 in the canopy above Rustpool Banks in Noctilum. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Desdemona, the Subterranean.

The Devil Mephite (Japanese: , Debiru Mepitesu) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Mephite and is fought at level 16 in the Whale's Nostril in Noctilum during the quest Data Miner.
Division Drive (Japanese: , Yunion Sutorīto, Union Street) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the Administrative District region of New Los Angeles.
Dilus (Japanese: , Kurogosu) are quadrupedal crocodile-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They tend to be found near waterways, and are similar to Tersquals.

Dieter, the Epicure (Japanese: , Bishoku no Dītā) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Grex family. It can be found at level 39 near Primordia's Talon Rock Second Terrane, directly above the entrance to the Beasts' Lair. It rests for a while before running through Sayram Northeast Plain to forage at the entrance of the Beasts' Lair, and then returns to the top. It must be defeated to complete the mission Dieter, the Epicure. It must also be hunted 5 times as one of the Squad Tasks for BLADE Mission No.18.
Delusians South Summit (Japanese: , Minami Meimō-san Chōjō) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, south of Hardheart Canyon and Gehenna Span.
Delusians North Summit BC (Japanese: , Kita Meimōsan Chōjō BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a BLADE base camp located in Sylvalum, on the Delusians North Summit.

The Devil's Colony (Japanese: , Debiruzu Koronī) is an area in . It is a cave located in Oblivia, in a cave southwest of the Twin Arches and directly south of FN Site 302. Bobby's Watch must be retrieved from here during Emotion Commotion, as must the Crimson Tear during The Ultimate Price.

Dirk (Japanese: , Diruku) is an NPC in . He is located at Division Drive in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. After Chapter 6 is completed he can be found at West Ciel Sandsea in Sylvalum where he will have a mission, after said mission is completed it will possible to find him at West Melville Street in the Commercial District during the night. He is a member of the Harriers Division.

Diogenes, the Covetous (Japanese: , Don'yokuna Diohenesu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Simius and can be found at level 28 south of Central Ibra Ravine in Oblivia. It must be defeated for Squad Mission No.3.
Doga Dandelions (Japanese: , Dogatanpopo) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia.

The Dimnet Xiphias (Japanese: , Rumederu Dimune) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Xiphias, and is fought at level 44 in the Behemoth's Shadows in Sylvalum during New in New LA.

The Disaster Vigent (Japanese: , Dizasutā Pekkā) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Vigent family, and is fought at level 40 on a mesa northwest of Silent Mire in Primordia during The Little Rich Girl. It does not have to be defeated to complete the mission, but if the player chooses to fight it, the Scrap Duo must be used to defeat it.

Dobromila, the Alluring (Japanese: , Yōka Doburomira) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Sacrifole family. It can be found at level 63 at the middle of the eastern part of Lake Ciel in Sylvalum. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Dobromila, the Alluring. It also must be defeated for BLADE Mission No.15.

Dodonga Caravan (English dub: ) (Japanese: , Dodonga Kyaraban) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Nopon caravan that was originally established by the Nopon leader Dodonga. It is located in Noctilum, inside Whale's Nostril by the southern entrance. The closest landmark is Old Dragontail Tree.
Doragaroos (Japanese: , Doragaru) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia.

Denemozumi Mice (Japanese: , Denemozumi) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular north of the FN Site 314. Eight of them are needed for Lab Rat Run.

Dobobora Broccolis (Japanese: , Dobobora Burokkorī) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular around North Coast and on the Floating Reef. Three heads are needed for The Ultimate Pursuit. A head of dobobora broccoli is rewarded for completing Mayday.
Dosoram Beans (Japanese: , Donramu Edamame) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
Diresheeps (Japanese: , Hitsujamo) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum. Six of them are needed for Hair Apparent.
Detilid Devices (Japanese: , Detiriddo Debaisu) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
Double Helical Salts (Japanese: , Nijūrasen no Soruto) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
Demon Boars (Japanese: , Inoshashi) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros' caves.
Doom Masks (Japanese: , Hyūman Heddo) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros.

Dithblade Fragments (Japanese: , Disuburēdo no Hahen) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros, in particular in the Ganglion Antropolis, the Ganglion Weapons Hangar or on the Cauldros Waters.

The Deva Caladar (Japanese: , Deva Kakara) is a Story Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Caladar, a Wrothian Skell piloted by Ga Buidhe, and is fought at level 34 at the Shivering Sands in Sylvalum. It assists Vasara, the Skell piloted by Ga Jiarg, during the final battle of Chapter 9. Level 40 versions of the Vasara and Deva Caladar can be fought in the Time Attack mission The Wrothian Samurai after completing Chapter 9. Skells cannot be used on this mission.

Den of the Dead (Japanese: , Mōja no Dōkutsu) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum. It is a hidden cave beneath the Delusians North Summit, accessable through moving directly east from FN Site 416 - the entrance is raised above ground level and accessable to Skells. The area contains many Caro and Milsaadi, including Lyla, the Lustrous.

Dopang Caravan (Japanese: , Dopān Kyaraban) is a Nopon Caravan in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, in Cleansing Spring area - unlike the other caravans, Dopang Caravan itself is not an area, landmark or location. It must be visited during Sparking a Smile.
Demetrio, the Tempestuous (Japanese: , Reppū no Demetorio) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Simius family. It can be found at level 28 at Ensconced Citadel in Noctilum.

Divine Liceors (Japanese: , Debain Kurāra) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Liceor family, and can be found at level 51-64 in Sylvalum. A group of three at levels 51 - 53 can be found on the Delusians South Summit, east of FN Site 419. A solitary one at level 52 can be found west of the FN Site. They can also be found in Sandsprint Cavity, surrounded by level 63 Uncanny Murra.

Diamond Blattas (Japanese: , Daiya Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 42-43 in the Behemoth's Shadows in Sylvalum. One of them is hiding on the wall in a tunnel.
Dismantler is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Striker at rank 10.
Dirty Fighter is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Shield Trooper at rank 9.
Double Spike is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Bastion Warrior at rank 9. Cross and H.B. can use this skill.
Double Reflect is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Bastion Warrior at rank 10. Cross and L can use this skill.

Dolba the Wrecker (Japanese: , Kowashiya Doruba) is Mission Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Human-Made Skell piloted by a Harrier named Dolba and can be found at level 43 at Sylvalum's North Cinderdunes. Battling it is required during Professorial.
Diamond Seeds are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Sacrifoles.

The Demise Ictus (Japanese: , Demaisu Manda) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Ictus family, and can be found at level 60 at Fallshorn Isle in Primordia. Defeating it is required during Then and Now. Its arts include Ether Shot (ether) and Roar (physical).
Dinner Discussion is Lin's fourth Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It occurs between Lin and Cross in the evening, at Barista Court in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.
Discipline and Discovery is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located at the Sports Complex in the Residential District of New Los Angeles between Doug and Cross during the day.

Departure's Eve is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Kun'luarb and the primary destination is the Residential District of New Los Angeles. Although not required to accept it, this mission leads into the Normal Mission The Journey Begins.

Dogged Obsession is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located south of the Water Purification Plant in the Residential District of New Los Angeles between Irina and Cross in the evening.
Distilled Sap is a rare material in . It can be obtained from Sylooth in several regions. They are required for Potential Up augments. One vial is required for The Next Big Thing.
Developed Balaena Fat are unique materials in . They can be obtained from Balaenas.
Dirty Work is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Prospectors and the primary destination is Cauldros.
The Deus-Crusher is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X.
Detonation-F is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is known as Bomb-Frail in the Japanese version.

Deva Caladar's Red Ears are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from the Deva Caladar, or for 210 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are also given out as rewards for completing the Time Attack mission The Wrothian Samurai. They are components for X, XV, and XX Ultrafauna Slayer and Slayer.ULTRAFAUNA augments.
Dirty Clothes are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Milsaadi.
Dilus A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a blue dilus variant. It can be obtained from Sarcosuchus, the Iron-Eater in Noctilum.
Dilus B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a brown dilus variant. It can be obtained from Sheldon, the Dentally Challenged in Oblivia.
Destined Encounter is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Zo Zazhi holding a cat. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission A Dish Served Cold.
Divine Custom is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts two female Tree Clan Prone. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission A New Life.

Diversional Tactics is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.10, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty Caecuses. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Doug's Bodywear is Medium Wear torso armor in and . It is manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group. It is part of Doug's initial gear when he joins the team, and cannot be obtained any other way.
The Dorian Treaty is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained as a reward after completing Dorian Caravan. It is required during the main mission BFFs.
The Dodonga Treaty is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained as a reward after completing Dodonga Caravan. It is required during the main mission BFFs.
Disguises are Casual Wear full-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. It's an upgraded version of the Party Suit.
Diving Bodywear are Casual Wear torso armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
The Distinguished Uniform is Casual Wear full-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. Only one can be obtained per playthrough.
Delta Thwippers are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Sniper Rifles. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 264,000 Credits.
Delta Triggers are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Sniper Rifles. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 33,000 Credits.
Delta Strobes are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Rayguns. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 330,000 Credits.
Delta Ruina III are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Psycho Launchers. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 363,000 Credits.
Delta Saboteurs are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Psycho Launchers. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 302,500 Credits.
Delta Sclopetums are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Assault Rifles. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 330,000 Credits.
Delta Sicariuses are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Sniper Rifles. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 396,000 Credits.
Delta Sniper Rifles are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Sniper Rifles. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 330,000 Credits.
Delta Sniper Rifles II are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Sniper Rifles. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 330,000 Credits.
Delta Ziyses are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Gatling Guns. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 321,700 Credits.
Delta Zorcyses are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Psycho Launchers. They can be purchased from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 272,200 Credits.

The Diagonal Twins are a one-of-a-kind melee weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Dual Swords. They are acquired during the Normal Mission That's In-Credible! and must be used to defeat Quick Evellos. They must be returned to Tutura after the enemies have been defeated. This weapon cannot be sold, nor can any augment slots be added to them.
Doug's Legwear is Medium Wear leg armor in and . It is manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group. It is part of Doug's initial gear when he joins the team, and cannot be obtained any other way.
Doug's Armwear L is Medium Wear left arm armor in and . It is manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group. It is part of Doug's initial gear when he joins the team, and cannot be obtained any other way.
Doug's Armwear R is Medium Wear right arm armor in and . It is manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group. It is part of Doug's initial gear when he joins the team, and cannot be obtained any other way.
Diving Masks are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Diving Band Ls are Casual Wear left arm armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries, and are in set with the Diving Band R, Diving Mask, and Diving Bodywear.
Diving Band Rs are Casual Wear right arm armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries, and are in set with the Diving Band L, Diving Mask, and Diving Bodywear.

Dialek Glyphs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Level 50-59 Unique Monsters. According to their description, the truth of logic is inscribed on them and like every glyph, they sell for a high price on the market.
Dorothy (Japanese: , Dorotea) is a Homs in . She is a member of the Defence Force, and can be found near Dunban's House in Colony 9.

Division Points, also known as DP, are an important mechanic in . They are earned by performing various BLADE-related activities, such as completing Missions, defeating Enemies, planting Data Probes, or gathering Collectibles. When enough DP are earned, Cross's BLADE Level will increase. The amount of DP earned is greater when the activity is related to Cross's current Division. For example, Pathfinders are responsible for planting Data Probes, and will earn more DP than other divisions do for that activity. When playing online, Division Points were also used to determine the daily global ranking of each division, with all players in a division contributing to their division's score. This me
Denden is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who can be found at the Argentum Bazaar in the Argentum Trade Guild, where he runs a shop called Shroomblade Smithing. Denden offers no quests or Merc missions.
Dockle Paguls (Japanese: , Togetsuno Pagūru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. They are members of the Pagul family, and can be found at level 3 in the Ancient Ship. This enemy drops no items.
Diamond Oak are Key Items in . They can be found at Dawnview Grotto in the Gormott Province. Five pieces are needed for Umon's Ship.
